problems.title: A triangle base from its altitude and base angles
problems.question: In triangle ABC, angle A=α, angle C=γ, and altitude BH=h. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use the two right triangles made by the altitude.
formulas: AH=h cot α; HC=h cot γ, using directed projections when an angle is obtuse.
steps: Add the projections along AC. The directed version also covers an altitude foot outside the segment.

problems.title: Recognize a point on the unit circle
problems.question: Which listed point always lies on the unit circle?
problems.idea: Its two squared coordinates must sum to 1.
steps: For (cos75°,−cos15°), the squared-coordinate sum is cos²75°+sin²75°=1.

problems.title: Convert a cosine to a sine
problems.question: Which listed α can satisfy $\cos(2\pi/5)=\sin(\pi/5-\alpha)$?
problems.idea: Use complementary angles.
steps: Setting π/5−α=π/10 gives α=π/10, which is listed and works.
More generally sin u=sin v gives u=v+2kπ or u=π−v+2kπ.

problems.title: How many lines through one point can make 60° with each other?
problems.question: Find the maximum number of distinct lines through a point in 3D such that every pair makes angle 60°.
problems.idea: Three examples exist along three edges of a regular tetrahedron from one vertex; rule out four.
steps: Three tetrahedron-edge lines give a construction. Suppose four lines were possible. Orient their unit directions so the last three each have dot product 1/2 with the first.
Their normalized projections onto the plane perpendicular to the first direction would have pairwise dot products 1/3 or −1.
If two projections are opposite, a third cannot have dot products in {1/3,−1} with both. If no two are opposite, all three pairwise dot products equal 1/3.
But three planar vectors cannot have that Gram matrix: its determinant is (1−1/3)²(1+2/3)=20/27>0, which would require three independent vectors. Thus four lines are impossible.

problems.title: Parallel lines preserve perpendicular directions
problems.question: Choose a universally true triple in: if a and b are …, and b and c are …, then a and c are … .
problems.idea: Parallel lines have the same direction.
formulas: If u∥v and v·w=0, then u·w=0.
steps: Therefore a∥b and b⊥c imply that the directions of a and c are perpendicular.
problems.note: In space this uses perpendicularity of directions (angle between lines), as in the test. If perpendicular lines are required to intersect, the intersection condition must also be supplied.

problems.title: Evaluate standard trigonometric values
problems.question: Evaluate $4\cos(\pi/3)-6\sin(\pi/6)+\sqrt2\sin(3\pi/4)-\tan(3\pi/4)$.
problems.idea: Use the standard values at 30°,60°,135°.
steps: The expression is 2−3+1−(−1)=1.

problems.title: Angle measures versus numerical coefficients
problems.question: Which of A=(π/5)cosα−36cosα, B=cos(π/5)−cos36°, C=(π/3)cos60°−60cos(π/3) is identically zero?
problems.idea: Radians and degrees can name the same angle, but numerical coefficients remain different numbers.
steps: B=0 because its cosines have equal arguments.
A=(π/5−36)cosα is not identically zero, although it vanishes for some α.
C=(π/3−60)/2 is nonzero.
problems.note: If the wording merely asks which expressions can be zero, A can also vanish when cosα=0. “Identically zero” is the intended interpretation.

problems.title: A sine difference in disguise
problems.question: Evaluate cos13° sin43°+sin167° cos137°.
problems.idea: Replace supplementary-angle trig values.
formulas: sin167°=sin13°; cos137°=−cos43°; sin(u−v)=sin u cos v−cos u sin v.
steps: The expression becomes sin43° cos13°−cos43° sin13°=sin30°.

problems.title: Possible angles between three skew lines
problems.question: Three pairwise skew lines have angles 55° between a,b and 15° between b,c. Which listed value can be the angle between a,c?
problems.idea: Positions determine skewness; directions determine the angles.
formulas: The direction angle between a and c can vary continuously from 55°−15° to 55°+15°.
steps: Thus the permitted interval is [40°,70°].
Of the listed 10°,15°,35°,65°,75°,90°, only 65° lies in this interval.
The lines can be translated to make them pairwise skew without altering directions.

problems.title: Angle between projections of two equal oblique segments
problems.question: Two equal segments from a point to a plane make 30° with the plane and 60° with each other. Find the cosine of the angle between their projections.
problems.idea: Split each segment into a vertical component and an in-plane component.
formulas: For length L: height=L/2, projection length=L√3/2; u·v=L² cos60°.
steps: The dot product of the projections equals L²/2−(L/2)²=L²/4.
Divide by their length product 3L²/4.

problems.title: Combine double-angle identities
problems.question: Evaluate cos²20° cos5°−2cos20°sin20°sin5°−sin²20°cos5°.
problems.idea: Group the first and last terms.
formulas: cos²t−sin²t=cos2t; 2sin t cos t=sin2t; cos(u+v)=cos u cos v−sin u sin v.
steps: The expression is cos40°cos5°−sin40°sin5°=cos45°.

problems.title: Simplify a trigonometric fraction
problems.question: Simplify cosα tanα+cos²α/(1+sinα).
problems.idea: Use cos²α=(1−sinα)(1+sinα).
steps: On the original domain, cosα≠0 and 1+sinα≠0.
The sum is sinα+1−sinα=1.
problems.answer: 1, wherever the original expression is defined.

problems.title: Reduce large angles before ordering
problems.question: Order $A=\cos(25\pi/7)$, $B=\tan(9\pi/7)$, $C=17\pi/2$ increasingly.
problems.idea: Reduce using cosine’s period 2π and tangent’s period π.
steps: 0<A<1 because 3π/7 is between 0 and π/2.
1<B<√3 because 2π/7 lies between π/4 and π/3.
C=17π/2 is greater than 2.

problems.title: A point equidistant from three triangle vertices
problems.question: M is distance 13 from each vertex of a right triangle with legs 6 and 8. Find its distance from the triangle’s plane.
problems.idea: Its perpendicular projection is the circumcentre.
steps: The required distance is the nonnegative square root.

problems.title: Lines in two perpendicular planes
problems.question: Perpendicular planes meet along AB. C is in one plane and D in the other, with angles CAB=DAB=45°. Find the smaller angle between AC and AD.
problems.idea: Resolve both directions along the common line and perpendicular to it.
steps: Their dot product is 1/2. Signs of the perpendicular components do not change that value.
Thus the angle is arccos(1/2).

problems.title: A fourth-power difference
problems.question: Find (sin⁴α−cos⁴α)/(cosα sinα) if tanα=2.
problems.idea: Factor the difference of squares and cancel using sin²+cos²=1.
steps: Substitute tanα=2 and cotα=1/2.

problems.title: A cancelled denominator changes an endpoint
problems.question: For which a does (2cos²α−1)/(cosα+sinα)=√a have a real solution?
problems.idea: Factor the numerator, but retain the denominator restriction.
steps: The quotient equals cosα−sinα where cosα+sinα≠0.
Although cosα−sinα ranges over [−√2,√2], both endpoints occur only when cosα+sinα=0, which is forbidden.
Thus the actual range is (−√2,√2). A nonnegative √a belongs to it exactly when 0≤a<2.
problems.note: The printed interval [0,2] wrongly includes a=2, where every candidate makes the original denominator zero.

problems.title: Add two complementary acute angles
problems.question: sin(α+β)=4/5, sin(α−β)=3/5, and α,β,α+β are acute. Find sin2α.
problems.idea: Both α+β and α−β are acute, so their cosines are positive.
formulas: cos(α+β)=3/5; cos(α−β)=4/5; sin(u+v)=sin u cos v+cos u sin v.
steps: Set u=α+β,v=α−β. Then u+v=2α.

problems.title: Similar right triangles sharing an altitude
problems.question: From A to a plane, oblique segments AB:AC=3:4 have projection lengths BH,CH differing by 7. Triangles ABH and CAH are similar. Find AH.
problems.idea: The unequal hypotenuses force the similarity to swap the two legs.
formulas: Let BH=u, CH=v, AH=h. Then h²=uv and AB²/AC²=u/v.
steps: u/v=9/16 and v−u=7, giving u=9,v=16.

problems.title: A plane through a rhombus side
problems.question: A plane through a rhombus side makes angles 30° and 60° with the diagonals. Find the acute angle of the rhombus.
problems.idea: Use perpendicular diagonal directions and a unit normal to the plane.
formulas: The absolute normal components along the diagonals are sin30°=1/2 and sin60°=√3/2.
steps: Their squares sum to 1, so the normal lies in the rhombus plane. It is perpendicular to the side where the planes meet.
If half-diagonals are p,q, perpendicularity to the side gives p/2=q√3/2, up to swapping the diagonals. Thus the longer:shorter diagonal ratio is √3:1.
A rhombus diagonal bisects its angle, so tan(acute angle/2)=1/√3.

problems.title: A bounded infinite arithmetic progression
problems.question: The sequence 0,sinα,sin2α,sin3α,… is an arithmetic progression. What must follow?
problems.idea: An infinite arithmetic progression of nonzero difference is unbounded.
formulas: Its terms here all lie in [−1,1].
steps: Its common difference must therefore be zero. The first term is 0, so sinα=0.
Thus α=kπ and cos2α=cos2kπ=1.

problems.title: A periodic function involving the floor
problems.question: Which listed function is periodic: x+sin x, ⌊cos x⌋, x sin x, (1/x)cos(1/x), {x²}, or ⌊x⌋²?
problems.idea: Applying the same fixed rule to a periodic function preserves its periods.
steps: Consequently ⌊cos(x+2π)⌋=⌊cos x⌋, so 2π is a period.
The polynomial-growth alternatives cannot repeat unchanged; {x²} also has no fixed positive period, since 2Tx+T² cannot be an integer for every real x.

problems.title: The largest distance between two trig-coordinate points
problems.question: A=(sinα,cosα), B=(cosα,sinα). Find the greatest AB.
problems.idea: Compute the squared distance.
steps: Since sin2α≥−1, AB²≤4.
Equality is possible, for example at α=−π/4.

problems.title: How many cube vertices determine its centre?
problems.question: A point is equally distant from some cube vertices. How many vertices guarantee that the point is the cube centre?
problems.idea: Four selected vertices might all lie in one face; five cannot all be coplanar.
formulas: Equal squared distances to vᵢ,vⱼ imply X·(vᵢ−vⱼ)=0 after placing the cube centre at the origin.
steps: Four vertices in a face allow any point on that face’s perpendicular central line, so four do not guarantee the cube centre.
A plane contains at most four cube vertices. Thus any five selected vertices span 3D affinely.
Their difference vectors span all three directions, forcing X=0.
problems.answer: 5 vertices for a guarantee regardless of which vertices are chosen.
problems.note: Four noncoplanar vertices already suffice if that placement is specified; the worst-case guarantee requires five.

problems.title: A dihedral angle along a hexagon diagonal
problems.question: M is distance 2 from every vertex of a regular hexagon of side 1. Find the cosine of the angle between the hexagon plane and the plane through M and a short diagonal.
problems.idea: Project M to the hexagon centre O, then take a section perpendicular to the diagonal.
formulas: Hexagon circumradius=1; MO=√(2²−1²)=√3; distance from O to a short diagonal=1/2.
steps: If H is the midpoint of the short diagonal, the dihedral angle is MHO.
The right triangle has OH=1/2, MO=√3 and MH=√13/2.
Its cosine is OH/MH.
